hungary/buda-castle.name: Buda Castle, Fisherman Bastion and Matthias Church
hungary/buda-castle.description: The castle district above the Danube, with the fairytale Bastion and a gothic church.
hungary/buda-castle.details: Castle Hill has the royal palace housing the National Gallery and History Museum, the neo-Romanesque Fisherman Bastion and Matthias Church with its tiled roof. The funicular or a stroll up from the Chain Bridge leads to it. Views of Parliament across the river are the highlight.

hungary/budapest-baths.name: Szechenyi and Gellert thermal baths
hungary/budapest-baths.description: Budapest historic thermal baths, a soak in warm mineral pools.
hungary/budapest-baths.details: Szechenyi in City Park is a yellow neo-baroque complex with outdoor pools, and Gellert is an art nouveau bathhouse with a mosaic hall. Evening party baths are on some Saturdays. Bring a swimsuit and flip-flops, and book fast-track tickets in busy seasons.

hungary/parliament-danube.name: Parliament and a Danube cruise
hungary/parliament-danube.description: The neo-Gothic Parliament building and an evening boat trip when it is lit.
hungary/parliament-danube.details: The Hungarian Parliament is one of the largest in Europe, and guided tours inside need advance tickets. A Danube cruise at dusk passes the lit Castle, Chain Bridge and Parliament. The Shoes on the Danube memorial is a moving stop along the bank.

hungary/market-ruin-bars.name: Great Market Hall and ruin bars
hungary/market-ruin-bars.description: A covered market for paprika, langos and salami, and the famous bars in derelict buildings.
hungary/market-ruin-bars.details: The Great Market Hall has stalls of paprika, sausages and Tokaji wine, with langos (fried bread) on the upper floor. The ruin bars of the Jewish Quarter, such as Szimpla Kert, are quirky courtyards with mismatched furniture, best from the evening.

hungary/szentendre-danube-bend.name: Szentendre and the Danube Bend
hungary/szentendre-danube-bend.description: An artists town of baroque lanes and the river bend with Visegrad fortress.
hungary/szentendre-danube-bend.details: Szentendre is 30 minutes from Budapest by suburban train, with galleries, a marzipan museum and cobbled streets. Further on, Visegrad has a citadel with a view over the Danube bend and Esztergom has the great basilica. Boats also run in summer.

hungary/eger.name: Eger castle and the Valley of the Beautiful Women
hungary/eger.description: A baroque town with a castle that resisted the Ottomans, and cellars of Bull Blood red wine.
hungary/eger.details: Eger Castle holds a museum of the 1552 siege. The old town has a minaret, a basilica and thermal baths. The Szepasszony Valley is a row of wine cellars where you taste Egri Bikaver. Try several small glasses and then walk.

hungary/tokaj.name: Tokaj wine region
hungary/tokaj.description: A UNESCO wine landscape of volcanic hills and sweet Tokaji Aszu.
hungary/tokaj.details: Tokaj makes the sweet wine called the wine of kings. Cellar visits are in small producers, many cut into the hillside. It is about two hours from Eger and a long day trip from Budapest, so a car or driver helps. Harvest runs in autumn.

hungary/balaton-tihany.name: Lake Balaton and Tihany
hungary/balaton-tihany.description: Central Europe largest lake, with a beach resort north shore and a lavender abbey peninsula.
hungary/balaton-tihany.details: Lake Balaton is shallow and warm in summer, with beaches at Balatonfured and Siofok. Tihany has an abbey, craft shops and lavender in June and July. Cycling the shore path or taking a ferry across the lake are summer pleasures. In winter the area is quiet.

hungary/pecs-zsolnay.name: Pecs and the Zsolnay Quarter
hungary/pecs-zsolnay.description: A southern city of early Christian tombs, a mosque-church and ceramic works.
hungary/pecs-zsolnay.details: Pecs has a UNESCO set of early Christian burial chambers, the Mosque Church on the main square and the Zsolnay Cultural Quarter, home of colourful ceramics. It is milder than Budapest. The city is about 3 hours by train from the capital.
